Notes on [Causal Inference for the Brave and
True](https://matheusfacure.github.io/python-causality-handbook/) plus
supplementary sources, written while working through the material.

The goal is not to restate the textbook but to **retain** it. So every chapter
ends not with conclusions but with a check: a simulation where the true effect
is known in advance, and an estimator that has to recover it.

## How a chapter works

Every chapter follows the same seven steps. The order is deliberate: intuition
before formalism, code before the explorable, own words last.

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | **The question** — what problem the chapter solves, in one sentence |
| 2 | **Intuition** — before any math |
| 3 | **Formalism** — the estimand and the assumptions it needs |
| 4 | **Verify with code** — a simulation with known ground truth |
| 5 | **Explorable** — break an assumption with a slider, watch the bias appear |
| 6 | **When it breaks** — failure modes and diagnostics |
| 7 | **In my own words** — a summary written without looking back |

Step 4 carries the weight. In real data the counterfactual is never observed,
so there is nothing to check an estimator against. In a simulation it *is*
observed, because we defined both potential outcomes ourselves. If the
estimator returns the effect we planted, the estimator is understood. If it
does not, we have learned exactly what we do not understand.

## Three kinds of interactivity

Interactivity on this site comes in three grades, and they differ in cost:

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Baked charts

Heavy analysis runs at build time in real Python and R, and reaches the page
as finished interactive Plotly. Hovering and zooming are instant; the
parameters are fixed.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Live code

Cells in the [lab](labs/index.qmd) execute in the browser through
WebAssembly. The code can be edited and re-run with no server involved. The
first run pays a few seconds to boot the engine.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Explorables

[Sliders and charts](explorables/index.qmd) in plain JavaScript. They respond
with no delay — and intuition about a parameter only forms when the response
is immediate.
:::

:::

## How this is built

Quarto plus GitHub Pages. Cell output is cached in `_freeze/` and committed, so
CI runs neither Python nor R — it only assembles HTML from finished results.
The reasoning behind each decision is in
[ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/ivan-stetsiuk/causal-inference-playbook/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md).
